🎙 Iran officials congratulate wrestlers on U23 World Championships victory in US

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian officials, in separate messages, have congratulated the country’s Greco-Roman wrestling team on winning the U23 World Championships in the United States, praising the athletes’ determination and international achievement.

Iran claimed the title with three gold medals, two bronze medals and 119 points at the championships held in Las Vegas from October 12 to 18, finishing ahead of Kazakhstan and Russia.
​
First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref described the victory on US soil as a powerful expression of Iranian youth’s determination and belief in their abilities, saying the achievement embodied the spirit of “We can” and demonstrated that young Iranians could reach the highest levels through faith, talent and perseverance.
​
Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the wrestlers had brought honor to their country by winning the title in the United States. He praised their ability to defend Iran’s name and national flag on the international stage, attributing the team’s success to scientific management, purposeful planning, dedicated coaches and the athletes’ hard work.
​
Judiciary Chief Gholamhossein Mohseni-Ejei said that this great victory sent a clear and powerful message to the aggressive and arrogant US leadership, as the wrestlers proved that the Iranian will cannot be defeated on any soil or behind any barrier, and that the proud flag of the Islamic Republic of Iran can fly high with strength even in the heart of lands whose rulers claim global dominance.
​
Sports and Youth Minister Ahmad Donyamali also welcomed the championship, describing it as another demonstration of Iran’s standing in international wrestling. He highlighted the significance of success in youth competitions and congratulated the wrestlers, coaching staff, team officials and the Wrestling Federation.
​
Erfan Jarkani won gold in the 63kg category, Abolfazl Mehmedi in the 82kg division and Yasin Yazdi in the 87kg class. Mohammad Kamali secured bronze at 67kg, while Mohammad Hadi Seidi won bronze at 97kg.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, has congratulated nurses on Nurses’ Day, praising their historic contributions and dedication, particularly during the imposed wars.

​
He added that nurses had shown exemplary courage and commitment, risking their lives to save their compatriots despite the dangers of war, and had secured a lasting place in the Iranian nation’s memory.

⚡️ Pezeshkian: Iran will not allow US to achieve its sinister objectives

📌 Tabriz, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian says Iran will not allow the United States to achieve its sinister goals by disrupting the country’s supply routes and creating public discontent.

“The enemy is doing everything it can to prevent us from serving our dear people and to create public discontent, hoping that social protests will emerge and allow it to achieve its sinister objectives. But with the support of our producers, exporters and entrepreneurs, we will not allow the United States to achieve its sinister goal,” the president said on Thursday.
​
He made the remarks while speaking online at a meeting of East Azarbaijan Province’s Planning and Development Council in Tabriz.
​
Pezeshkian added that Iran remains resolute and would secure its needs through all available means, with the help of its people.
​
He also called on officials across the country to work together to resolve local problems, stressing that provinces should not rely solely on Tehran to address their challenges.
​
The president also praised the Armed Forces and defenders of the country for their resistance to enemy attacks, saying they accomplished a great and lasting feat. He said no power had expected them to withstand such massive attacks, adding that he was proud of each of them for defending the country with dedication despite all the hardships and shortages.
​
Public resilience foiled attempts to exploit Iran’s problems
​
Also on Thursday, President Pezeshkian addressed a ceremony marking Nurses Day in Tehran.
​
He said that the Iranian people thwarted adversaries’ plans to exploit the country’s economic, social and environmental challenges to undermine national cohesion.
​
He said adversaries had expected Iranian society to fall apart if the country came under attack, given its imbalances and problems.
​
Since the assassination of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh and the succession of crises that followed, he said, adversaries had sought to weaken national unity by fueling ethnic and gender tensions and exploiting domestic divisions.
​
He cited electricity shortages, water problems, budget imbalances, pension challenges and environmental issues, saying the public had stood firm and frustrated those plots. However, the president warned, adversaries continued to exploit these difficulties to sow discord.
